clue.text: Fix cost of entertaining northern nobleman

indicators.note: to entertain is to host someone, so the price phrase takes the northern letter inside it

parts.note: to fix the cost of something is to price it

explanation.surface: Someone settles the bill for hosting a lord from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a royal or high-ranking aristocrat, a type of nobleman.

clue.text: Philosopher with room to embrace fine policy

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the fine letter goes inside

parts.note: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A thinker who has space to accept a sensible approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform is a party's set of declared aims, its policy programme.

clue.text: Spiritual home

definitions.meaning: ... describes the inner, mental or spiritual life
... refers to the inside of a house, or a country's inland home territory

explanation.surface: A sacred dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior means inward or spiritual, and also the inside of a building or domestic affairs.

clue.text: Pacing, troubled about a mass crusade

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled word surrounds the next pieces
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Someone paces anxiously about a large holy war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges PACING to CAPIGN, which goes 'about' A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised drive for a cause, which is what a crusade is.

clue.text: Work quietly applied to hospital department for one's rival

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
something applied to a surface is on it
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A quiet job done in a hospital department somehow benefits a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is the person or side competing against you, so a rival.

clue.text: Authorisation for a significant assignment

parts.note: per means for each, for a, as in a pound per day
a mission is an important task one is sent on

explanation.surface: Getting authority for an important task.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is formal consent, which is what authorisation grants.

clue.text: Love to classify fruit

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to range is to arrange in classes or order

explanation.surface: Fond of sorting fruit into categories.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Start of easy question and answer on oddly lost matches

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the next word
oddly means take the first, third and later odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A quiz begins with an easy question, then answers about lost games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes LS from 'lost'. 'matches' looks like games but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that equals another matches it in value or quality.

clue.text: Definite article or beginning of yet unproven supposition

parts.note: the is the definite article in English grammar

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson on articles drifts into speculation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation not yet proved, a hypothesis.

clue.text: Eccentric aunt and mum mostly showing period of maturity

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and out of line, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: An odd aunt and a mother are mostly on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MUM to MU; 'Eccentric' then shuffles AUNT with MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is used figuratively for the mature later stage of life, after summer's prime.

clue.text: Make a fuss about old city animal

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the fuss word goes round the city

parts.note: to create is British slang for making a fuss or complaining loudly
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a fuss over an animal from an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Create' in British informal speech means to make a fuss, as in 'don't create'.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any living being, especially an animal.

clue.text: Shape nearly everything according to established style

parts.note: form means shape

indicators.note: nearly means not completely, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Shaping almost everything to fit the accepted style.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal describes what follows recognised conventions and etiquette rather than being casual.

clue.text: Strange offence; forced labour camp not good answer ultimately

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for good

parts.note: a gulag was a Soviet forced labour camp

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word answer

explanation.surface: An odd crime sentence: forced labour in a camp without a good answer in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from GULAG, leaving GULA; then R from 'answer ultimately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular can mean remarkable or odd, an older sense of peculiar.

clue.text: Foreign female gripped by a friend from Paris, a storyteller

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside, so the female letter goes within the French phrase

parts.note: un ami is French for a friend
a storyteller is jokingly a liar, one who tells stories

explanation.surface: A French friend holds on to a woman and turns out to be a fibber.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfamiliar means strange or not known, close to foreign in the sense of alien.

clue.text: Orangeries running wild, to sort out again

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Greenhouses for citrus have gone out of control and need tidying.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorganise is to arrange or structure something afresh.

clue.text: Feasible involving annual return that may change

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the two letters go inside the feasible word

parts.note: viable means feasible or workable
A is the abbreviation for annual
R is the abbreviation for return

explanation.surface: A workable plan including a yearly tax return that might be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable describes anything liable to vary or alter.

clue.text: Left gap for window

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a hole is a gap or opening

explanation.surface: A space was left for a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is a small round window in a ship's side.

clue.text: One has one of them, and seven two

definitions.text: One has one of them, and seven two

parts.words: One has one of them, and seven two
parts.note: the words one and seven are counted by their spoken beats: one has a single beat, seven has two

explanation.surface: A riddle about counting something in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word one is spoken in a single unit of sound, seven in two units.

clue.text: Political party rhetoric in this workroom

parts.note: Lab is short for the UK Labour Party
oratory is the art of public speaking, rhetoric

explanation.surface: Party speechmaking taking place in this office.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab is the usual abbreviation for Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room equipped for scientific work and experiments.

clue.text: Subjects of inquiry involving university political movements

indicators.note: involving means including, so the university letter sits inside

parts.note: cases are matters investigated, as by police or courts

explanation.surface: Investigations into campus activism.
explanation.definitionFit: Causes are principles or movements that people campaign to support.

clue.text: In discussion, quote some local legends

indicators.note: some means only part of the words, so the answer is found within them

explanation.surface: Talking over a few stories passed down in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to state or cite something as a claim in argument.

clue.text: Improve quality of frolicking disheartened children

indicators.note: frolicking means playing about, so the letters are jumbled
disheartened means losing its heart, so the central letters are removed

explanation.surface: Cheering up sad children by letting them play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes LD from CHILDREN, leaving CHIREN, which 'frolicking' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to make something richer or better in quality.

clue.text: Main network found in roof space

indicators.note: found in says the network sits inside the roof space

parts.note: an attic is the space under a roof
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: The main computer network was discovered up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective but is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the ocean, and the Atlantic is an ocean.

clue.text: Gun plot is flawed

indicators.note: flawed means faulty, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A gun conspiracy has a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handheld firearm.

clue.text: Particular southern sports clubs regularly reversed coin flip

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sports
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: reversed means the picked letters are read backwards
regularly means taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: Southern sports clubs reversed a particular coin toss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes CIFI from 'coin flip'; 'reversed' turns it to IFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific means relating to one particular thing rather than in general.

clue.text: Take in brothers briefly returning after degree setback

indicators.note: after places the brothers piece behind the degree piece
set back means put in reverse, so the degree letters run backwards

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: returning means going back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: bros is the short form of brothers

explanation.surface: Absorbing a degree failure with the help of brothers coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns BA into AB; 'returning' turns BROS into SORB.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to soak up or take something into oneself.

clue.text: Guide essentially ineptly separating female and male on road

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the picked letter splits the two pronouns

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
he is a male pronoun

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clumsy guide comes between a woman and a man on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' asks for the heart of the word 'ineptly', its single central letter; 'separating' wedges that letter between the two pronouns, and 'on' just joins the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd is to guide or herd people along, as a shepherd leads a flock.

clue.text: Harsh to lop off earl's head

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Beheading an earl is a harsh punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means strict, stern or grim, a synonym of harsh.
